name: Why do homes in the Denver and Aurora area frequently develop drywall cracks and sticking doors?

mainEntity.name: Why do homes in the Denver and Aurora area frequently develop drywall cracks and sticking doors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dry climate conditions and seasonal temperature swings across the Denver metro area cause framing lumber to expand and contract, which frequently leads to hairline sheetrock cracks and popped drywall screws. Soil movement in areas like Parker, Centennial, and Aurora can also cause doors to stick and baseboard seams to separate. Regular maintenance involves refastening drywall to studs, taping and mudding joint cracks, and adjusting interior door jambs and molding to keep the home secure and aesthetically clean.
acceptedAnswer.description: Denver’s dry climate and expansive soils cause framing shifts, resulting in cracked drywall seams, popped screws, and misaligned interior doors that require routine upkeep.
